scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You place your phone on a pad, and it starts charging. No cable plugged in. So how does the power get in?

scenes.name: coil
scenes.text: Inside the pad is a flat coil of copper wire. Alternating current flowing through it creates a magnetic field that keeps changing.

scenes.name: induce
scenes.text: Your phone has a matching coil. The changing magnetic field passing through it induces an electric current. That's electromagnetic induction.

scenes.name: convert
scenes.text: That current is alternating, so a chip in the phone converts it into steady DC, to charge the battery.

scenes.name: talk
scenes.text: Under the Qi standard, the phone and pad communicate, agreeing on how much power to send, and spotting stray metal objects.

scenes.name: align
scenes.text: The coils need to line up. That's why some phones and pads use magnets, to snap into the right spot.

scenes.name: tradeoff
scenes.text: It's convenient, but some energy is lost as heat, so it's usually slower and a bit less efficient than a cable.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Coil, field, induction, battery. Power through the air. Follow for more on how things really work.
